concerns.location: research.md:Zero‑shot intent classifier with calibrated threshold
concerns.text: The zero‑shot intent classifier is calibrated on the deterministic rule‑based gold‑standard (50 samples) and, if κ ≥ 0.6, is used to score intent entities against that same gold set. This creates a circular validation: the predictor (classifier) is tuned on the very data that serves as the ground‑truth outcome, leading to data leakage and inflated intent‑preservation scores.

Phase 4 describes that if the calibrated classifier’s κ < 0.6 the pipeline falls back to the deterministic rule‑based extractor used to create the gold standard. In either case, intent evaluation relies on the same rule‑based definitions, so the metric does not independently assess the model’s ability to capture true technical intent but rather measures agreement with a self‑generated reference.
